name: Rubeus
what: A C# toolset for raw Kerberos interaction and abuse during an authorized Active Directory assessment. It performs ticket requests and renewals, Kerberoasting and AS-REP roasting, overpass-the-hash (pass-the-key), pass-the-ticket, ticket extraction from LSASS-free memory where possible, S4U constrained/resource-based delegation abuse, and golden/silver ticket forging when you already hold the relevant keys. It is the Windows-native counterpart to Impacket's Kerberos scripts.
when: On an internal or assumed-breach engagement with written scope, when you need to harvest roastable service accounts, convert an NT hash or AES key into a usable TGT, or exercise delegation paths that BloodHound flagged — all against a domain you own or are authorized to test.
example: Build from source or use your team's vetted build on an approved assessment host; record the commit you used.
Enumerate roastable accounts and request service tickets: `Rubeus.exe kerberoast /outfile:hashes.txt` (scope to specific SPNs rather than the whole domain to stay quiet).
AS-REP roast accounts without Kerberos pre-auth: `Rubeus.exe asreproast /format:hashcat /outfile:asrep.txt`, then crack offline with Hashcat.
Overpass-the-hash to obtain a TGT from a captured key: `Rubeus.exe asktgt /user:<svc> /aes256:<key> /ptt`, then act within scope.
Hand the SPNs, accounts and ticket activity to the blue team so Kerberos detections (roasting, encryption-downgrade, anomalous TGS requests) can be tuned.
pitfalls: You may only run this against systems you own or hold written authorization to test; Kerberos ticket abuse against others is illegal.
Kerberoasting at scale and RC4 encryption-type downgrades are noisy and trip modern detections (event 4769 patterns, Defender for Identity) — scope SPNs and agree thresholds with the SOC first.

Golden/silver ticket forging requires you to already possess the krbtgt or service key; it is a persistence/impact demonstration, not an initial-access exploit, and must be explicitly in the rules of engagement.
Keep cracked credentials, extracted tickets and keys in the engagement vault and wipe them at close.

sources.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1558: Steal or Forge Kerberos Tickets
